messages.content: You design amateur rockets that fly on certified commercial motors. Work through the design, check it with the tools, and give the final design as JSON inside <design> tags. Only report results the tools returned.
Design request. Must reach at least 2,000 ft. Soft landing, under 5.5 m/s. The airframe can't be wider than 2 inches. Please provide the full design.

messages.reasoning_content:
1. Understand: clear at least 2,000 ft, land under 5.5 m/s, and keep the airframe at or under 2 inches wide. No motor class and no stated wind or rail, so the defaults are a 1.5 m rail and 2 m/s of wind.
2. Feasibility: 2000 * 0.3048 = 610 m is a floor, not a target band. 2 * 0.0254 = 0.0508 m is the diameter cap. Vacuum speed for that altitude is sqrt(2 * 9.81 * 610) = 109 m/s, so with drag I want on the order of 80 to 120 N*s in a 29 mm case that fits the cap. Looking up an E, an F and a G.

2. Feasibility: the E12 is 27.1 N*s at 11.2 N, too little for 610 m. The G64W is 118.0 N*s and 0.1512 kg, more impulse than a minimum-altitude flight needs. The Estes F50 is 76.8 N*s at 55.8 N, 29 mm, 0.098 m long, 0.0836 kg, and the only delay is 6 s. The case fits under 0.0508 m. I will fly that.
3. Size: guessed liftoff mass 0.22 kg. Thrust-to-weight = 55.8 / (0.22 * 9.81) = 25.9. Pad weight 0.22 * 9.81 = 2.16 N, rail acceleration (55.8 - 2.16) / 0.22 = 244 m/s^2, exit speed sqrt(2 * 244 * 1.5) = 27.1 m/s. Descent mass 0.22 - 0.038 = 0.182 kg. At 4.5 m/s, under 5.5 m/s, area = 2 * 0.182 * 9.81 / (1.225 * 0.8 * 4.5^2) = 0.180 m^2, diameter sqrt(4 * 0.180 / 3.1416) = 0.479 m. I will pack 0.55 m. Burn 1.37 s plus the 6 s delay puts ejection near 7.4 s.
4. Draft: 0.10 m ogive polystyrene nose, 0.42 m cardboard tube at 0.041 m outer diameter and 1 mm wall. Mount 0.032 m outside and 0.12 m long, Estes F50 with a 6 s delay. Three balsa fins, root 0.090 m, tip 0.035 m, span 0.055 m, sweep 0.040 m, 3 mm thick. One 0.55 m ripstop chute on ejection.

4. Check: the altitude clears and the rocket is under-stable. The simulator gives 744.2 m, above 610 m, and landing 3.4 m/s, under 5.5 m/s. Diameter is 0.041 m, under 0.0508 m. Rail exit 35.7 m/s, thrust-to-weight 33.1. Margin is 0.77 cal at rail exit and through the burn, under 1.0 cal. The chute opens at 7.4 s, just before the 7.87 s apogee, at 18.1 m/s. Mass is 0.172 kg.
5. Fix: the failing value is 0.77 cal. Larger balsa fins: root 0.12 m, tip 0.045 m, span 0.075 m, sweep 0.055 m, still 3 mm. Motor, tube and chute stay. 744.2 - 610 = 134 m of altitude to spend on the extra drag.

4. Check: the fins helped and the margin is still short. The simulator gives 0.96 cal at rail exit and through the burn, under 1.0 cal. Apogee is 688.1 m, still above 610 m. Landing is 3.4 m/s. Rail exit 35.0 m/s, thrust-to-weight 32.3. The chute opens at 7.4 s, just before the 7.85 s apogee, at 13.6 m/s. Mass is 0.176 kg.
5. Fix: the failing value is 0.96 cal. Another fin increase would spend altitude I would rather keep. I am adding 0.005 kg of clay at the top of the tube to move the CG forward. Fins, motor and chute stay. Spare altitude is 688.1 - 610 = 78.1 m.

4. Check: the clay put the margin over the line. The simulator gives 1.13 cal at rail exit and through the burn. Apogee is 693.6 m, and 693.6 - 610 = 83.6 m over the floor. Landing is 3.5 m/s, under 5.5 m/s. The tube is 0.041 m, under 0.0508 m. Rail exit 34.2 m/s, thrust-to-weight 31.4. The chute opens at 7.4 s, just before the 7.87 s apogee, at 14.7 m/s. Mass is 0.181 kg.
5. Fix: no further change. Altitude, diameter, landing speed and the stability gates all pass.
6. Uncertainty: the F50 has only a 6 s delay, so the canopy opens slightly early at 14.7 m/s. There is no longer delay in the catalog. Margin is 1.13 cal. A heavier paint job still has 83.6 m of spare altitude. The 3.5 m/s landing assumes this 0.55 m chute is the one packed.
messages.content:
Estes F50-6 in a 41 mm cardboard airframe, inside the 2 inch limit, with larger balsa fins, 5 g of nose clay and a 0.55 m chute.
Apogee is 693.6 m, 83.6 m over the 610 m floor. Landing is 3.5 m/s, under 5.5 m/s. Margin is 1.13 cal.
The only F50 delay is 6 s, so the chute opens just before apogee at 14.7 m/s.
